title: Causal token trace mapper: real-time KV-influence and per-token chargeback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a streaming, low-overhead attribution layer that constructs causal token chains end-to-end across the serving runtime, so we can quantify per-token latency and cost including KV cache influence. This ticket implements: 1) a short-lived causal-id attached to request slices and token emissions; 2) lightweight in-memory token-span envelopes emitted by the runtime into our metrics/log pipeline; 3) a KV-influence model that flags cache-hit vs cache-fill segments and applies adjustable cost weights; 4) a real-time aggregation job to materialize per-request and per-customer token chargeback with configurable sampling. Deliverables: runtime hooks, protobuf envelope spec, ingestion transforms, sample Grafana dashboards, GitHub PRs, e2e test harness. Non-goals: full billing export (handled by a downstream billing job).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime attaches token_span_id for every emission with parent_request_id and batch_index
Ingestion pipeline decodes envelopes and persists token spans to the trace-store within 5s
KV-influence flag present for >99% of spans in canary runs
Per-request token cost report available in Grafana for a canary org
Overhead measured <2% p95 CPU on p3-small serving nodes in 1-hour load test
work_items: Define protobuf envelope and stable field names (proto link in comments)
Add attachment points in emission path and batching layer
Annotate existing KV cache API to surface hit/fill latencies
Instrument streaming transform to compute weighted token-time and tag cache influence
Dashboard + alerting for regressions and sample set release gating
